findings.description: Plan says convert-to-ralph-prd needs no edit, but skills/convert-to-ralph-prd/SKILL.md:396 still claims 'submodules initialize under the shared cross-process lock'. Under v5.50.0 default the helper does NOT init unless --init-submodules is passed; the Step 5 call omits the flag so this prose becomes false. Same stale claim in the Copilot mirror at .copilot-plugin/internal-workflows/convert-to-ralph-prd/SKILL.md:396.
findings.suggestedFix: Add convert-to-ralph-prd SKILL.md to MODIFY list: rewrite the bullet at line ~396 to read 'submodule init is OPT-IN via --init-submodules; this caller omits the flag so the impl worktree starts with uninitialized submodules. Members run git submodule update --init <path> on demand.' Regenerate the Copilot mirror via generate-copilot-artifacts.mjs.
findings.resolution: Added US-004b modifying convert-to-ralph-prd SKILL.md prose around line ~396; regenerate Copilot mirror; AC-6b covers grep verification.

findings.description: US-003 description is INACCURATE about the test file structure. tests/test-submodule-worktree-init.sh does NOT have CLI worktree-create.mjs cases to amend — its behavioral fixture uses inline `git worktree add` plus a sourced run_locked_submodule_update() helper that mirrors the decompose-plan Step 5b inline pattern. It asserts via assert_source_contract / assert_grep_contracts / assert_batch_scope that the source SKILL.md files contain certain init prose. Under v5.50.0, decompose-plan loses the init prose entirely, so assert_source_contract for decompose-plan AND the grep assertion for the Copilot mirror BOTH fail. Plan must redesign these assertions, not merely amend them.
findings.suggestedFix: Rewrite US-003 to: (a) drop assert_source_contract and assert_grep_contracts calls against decompose-plan SKILL.md and the Copilot mirror (those files no longer contain the init command). (b) Keep assert_source_contract / assert_grep_contracts against convert-to-ralph-prd SKILL.md and its Copilot mirror IF we decide convert-to-ralph-prd should keep some init reference for documentation traceability — but under v5.50.0, convert-to-ralph-prd ALSO loses any source claim that it inits, so these assertions ALSO need to be dropped or replaced with negative assertions. (c) Replace the behavioral fixture's run_locked_submodule_update() invocation against decompose-plan-style worktrees with CLI invocations of worktree-create.mjs against the existing super-repo fixture — one default-no-op case (asserting submoduleInitRan: false + empty submodules + no lock activity) and one --init-submodules case (asserting submoduleInitRan: true + populated submodules).
findings.resolution: Rewrote US-003 with explicit Test redesign subsection enumerating drop assertions / new negative assertions / new CLI cases / fixture repurpose.

findings.description: Test fixture's local submodule setup uses `git -c protocol.file.allow=always` per-call on every git invocation that touches the file:// submodule URL. worktree-create.mjs's runSubmoduleInit() runs plain `git submodule update --init --recursive` without the -c flag, so a new CLI opt-in test against the file:// fixture submodule will fail with 'transport file disallowed' on default Git ≥2.38 unless the fixture sets `protocol.file.allow=always` at the super-repo config level (so the worktree inherits it for the helper's plain git invocation).
findings.suggestedFix: US-003 fixture-setup step must add `git -C $SUPER_REPO config protocol.file.allow always` immediately after super-repo init (before submodule add). The worktrees created via worktree-create.mjs against this super-repo inherit the config setting, so the helper's plain `git submodule update --init --recursive` works without modification. Alternatively, expose a new env-var on worktree-create.mjs to inject -c — but operator excluded env-var handling, so the super-repo config approach is preferred.
findings.resolution: Added explicit fixture-setup step in US-003 step 1: git -C SUPER_REPO config protocol.file.allow always; documented in Test redesign subsection.

findings.description: AC-13 is post-merge, lead-owned smoke work. An autonomous impl member cannot satisfy it before the toolkit and codexu pointer commits are FF-merged. AC-13 also uses 'meaningfully faster than v5.49.0' without a numeric threshold or fixed baseline command — not objectively testable.
findings.suggestedFix: Move AC-13 out of the Acceptance Criteria list into a new 'Lead-Owned Post-Ship Smoke' section that explicitly states it is NOT a gate on impl completion. The impl member ships when AC-1..AC-12 + AC-14 + AC-15 pass; the lead runs the smoke after FF-merging and records it as advisory. Drop the 'meaningfully faster' wording — make the smoke note just 'submoduleInitRan: false observed in staging worktree-result.json + plan completed without referencing missing submodule code'.
findings.resolution: Moved AC-13 out of Acceptance Criteria into new Lead-Owned Post-Ship Smoke section explicitly NOT a gate on impl. Dropped meaningfully faster wording.

findings.description: Line numbers in plan are off. finishResult is at lines 132-144 (not 132 as claimed); parseArgs is at 146-178; runSubmoduleInit starts at line 263 (not 263-300 — extends to 300). Reuse-path call is line 92 (correct), but the 'lock acquired' line is 274 (not 271 as claimed).
findings.suggestedFix: Drop most line numbers from the plan — they're load-bearing only for impl members who'd otherwise grep, and they go stale on the first whitespace/import edit. Keep symbolic anchors (function names, switch case neighbors) and let the impl member find the exact lines. Where line ranges are kept (e.g. for the test file's existing case set), use approximate ranges with '~' prefix.
findings.resolution: Dropped most load-bearing line numbers from plan prose; kept symbolic anchors. Where ranges retained use ~ prefix.

findings.description: US-008 (codexu submodule pointer bump) cannot be done in the same autonomous impl session as US-001..US-007. It depends on the lead FF-merging the toolkit topic branch + pushing toolkit-main first. Plan's 'direct serial invocation' next-step language is misleading: one autonomous impl member can complete US-001..US-007 and then must hand off.
findings.suggestedFix: Move US-008 to a dedicated 'Lead-Owned Follow-Up' subsection of Implementation Strategy. State clearly: 'The autonomous impl member completes US-001..US-007 and reports kind=done. The lead executes the canonical Multi-repo wrapper-to-submodule ship ceremony (plugins/ralph/AGENTS.md), then either runs US-008 by hand or spawns a brief follow-up impl member to commit the codexu pointer bump.' Update the Next Step section accordingly.
findings.resolution: Added Lead-Owned Follow-Up subsection under Implementation Strategy explicitly stating US-008 cannot be done in same autonomous session. Updated Next Step section.
